A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–E. The retained material can be matched across pagination, figure renumbering, and restructuring.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original Gaussian-process generation experiments, covariance-estimation errors, and analyses of learned attention matrices.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional bouncing-ball video results, a UNet comparison, and network-size and training-dynamics experiments.

M1.justification: The core DiT and gradient-descent unrolling approach remains. v2 corrects the GD linear-term sign and modifies the constructed block to preserve the iterate separately before adding the rescaled gradient increment (Appendix B.3.2). Section 6.2 also adds a trained, frozen VAE encoder/decoder for applying DiT to latent video sequences.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic Gaussian-process sequences only. v2 retains these and adds semi-synthetic 64×64 bouncing-ball videos in Section 6.2, introducing image-sequence generation with wall collisions and non-Gaussian dynamics. The sequence-length sweeps remain within the existing Gaussian-process coverage.

E2.justification: v1 has no evaluated learned-model comparator; UNet appears only in background discussion. Appendix D.2 and Figure 11 of v2 introduce a direct comparison with UNet-based diffusion using approximately matched model sizes, adding the paper's first architectural baseline experiment.

E3.justification: The original covariance-decay and training-sample sweeps retain their settings and metric. New protocols include a 400-epoch DiT/UNet comparison with 10,000 training sequences and 10,000 generated evaluation samples per model, sequence lengths 16–256, depths 1–16, and training checkpoints at 1, 10, 50, and 100 epochs. These are added experiments, not documented reruns of the original results.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained covariance-decay and attention-layer diagnostics, v2 adds sequence-length and network-depth sensitivity analyses in Figure 12. Figure 13 examines when spatial and temporal dependencies emerge during training, addressing a different question from v1's analysis across backward denoising steps.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains its shaded bands, and the new Figure 12 uses similarly shaded curves without introducing an explained uncertainty-estimation procedure. Neither version specifies seed or repeated-run counts, defines the bands statistically, or reports significance tests.

E6.justification: The original Gaussian-process results are retained. New findings include covariance recovery and coherent bouncing-ball motion in Figures 6–7, better dependency recovery by DiT than UNet in Figure 11, depth saturation and sequence-length sensitivity in Figure 12, and earlier acquisition of spatial patterns than temporal correlations in Figure 13. These are additional results under new settings.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and their principal bounds are retained. v2 corrects the Gaussian-score sign and corresponding quadratic/GD formulas in Equations 2–4 and several appendix derivations, and revises the constructive proof's state handling. Assumption 1 changes 'strictly increasing' to 'increasing'; Section 2 replaces strict-stationarity wording with a condition on lag-dependent covariance.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged, and the introduction retains the same contributions: transformer score approximation through algorithm unrolling, sample-complexity guarantees, and empirical recovery of spatial-temporal dependencies. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a connection to Gaussian VAE latent priors, a conjecture linking UNet's piecewise correlations to convolutional filters, and interpretations of the new scaling and training-dynamics results. Appendix B.5 additionally claims reduced transformer depth with softmax. The original Gaussian-modeling limitation and proposed extension to generic dynamics remain.

D1.justification: The existing patch-embedding and covariance-estimation details are retained. Added disclosures include VAE pretraining on 20,000 frames followed by freezing and latent-video training, the UNet's four down/up stages with three residual/convolution layers per stage, and Adam with batch size 128 for the training-dynamics experiment.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and positioning around latent video diffusion, Gaussian-process VAEs, and financial or discrete sequential data, including Rombach, Blattmann, Wang, Casale, Fortuin, Gao, and Campbell and colleagues. The central positioning of the work as a theory of diffusion transformers for Gaussian-process sequences remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introductory and terminology edits, distinguishes diffusion timesteps from data time indices, adds an assumptions overview before Appendix A, and expands construction explanations. Section 6 and Appendix D gain subsections separating retained and additional experiments; the overall argument and proof organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 6–7 and 11–13, including video frames, baseline heatmaps, scaling curves, and training trajectories. Figure 5 is compressed and rearranged, while the complete attention analysis remains in renumbered Figure 10. Tables 1–4 largely convert existing network-size lists into structured displays, substantially expanding and reorganizing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Corrected main score/GD equations and the new baseline, scaling, training-dynamics, and non-Gaussian video experiments improve correctness and empirical support. However, sign inconsistencies persist, including Lemma 11 versus Equation 14. The new Table 4 discussion also compares a per-iteration softmax block count with the full-network count in Table 3. These mathematical clarity problems temper the added evidence, yielding a limited net improvement.
